issues.body: `pipefail_delta` is still called on individual physical-line segments. For `set +o pipefail`, followed by `set -o \\` on one physical line and `pipefail` on the next, bash re-enables pipefail, but the scanner sees neither physical line as a complete enable and retains `pipefail = False`. It then blanks a subsequent `producer | head -1` shape, allowing the real-workflow assertion to return a false-clean zero. The new exact-count fixture has no backslash-continuation positive control, so it does not catch this bypass.
issues.fix_hint: Track option transitions over shell logical commands, including backslash continuations, before deciding whether subsequent commands are emitted. Add a fixture that disables pipefail, re-enables it using `set -o \\` plus `pipefail` on the next physical line, then runs a vulnerable pipeline, and require that pipeline to be counted.
issues.title: Backslash-continued pipefail re-enable still bypasses the workflow guard

verdict.summary: The round-3 major finding remains unresolved. `_workflow_run_shell` still evaluates each physical line independently, so a backslash-continued `set -o pipefail` executed by bash is not recognized by `pipefail_delta`. The fixture adds same-line separator controls but no multiline logical-command control. Consequently the guard can still suppress a later vulnerable pipeline and report a false-clean zero.
